llm-apis.name: Google Gemini API
llm-apis.description: Frontier multimodal models on a permanent free tier — Flash and Flash-Lite families only since April 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,500 requests/day on Flash, 1,000/day on Flash-Lite; 250K TPM
llm-apis.notes: Free-tier prompts are used to improve Google products outside the EU/UK/EEA. Pro models left the free tier in April 2026.

llm-apis.name: Groq Cloud
llm-apis.description: Open-weight models at 300+ tokens/sec on LPU hardware, with the most generous request-per-day allowance of any free tier.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,000 req/day and 200K tokens/day per model
llm-apis.notes: The 200K tokens/day ceiling usually binds before the request count does. Llama models were removed from the free plan in 2026.

llm-apis.name: OpenRouter Free Models
llm-apis.description: One OpenAI-compatible key fronting 19+ `:free` models across providers — the best way to A/B models without multiple signups.
llm-apis.free_limit: 50 requests/day (1,000/day after a one-time $10 credit purchase)
llm-apis.notes: The `:free` roster rotates monthly. Upstream providers frequently return 429s on free variants.

llm-apis.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
llm-apis.description: Serverless inference that runs inside a Worker — no egress cost, no cold-start management, free daily budget.
llm-apis.free_limit: 10,000 Neurons/day (roughly 3-8K short LLM calls/day)
llm-apis.notes: Budget is denominated in Neurons, not tokens — per-model conversion varies, so budget by testing one call.

llm-apis.name: GitHub Models
llm-apis.description: Frontier and open models behind a GitHub PAT — the lowest-friction free tier if you already have a GitHub account.
llm-apis.free_limit: 150-1,000 requests/day depending on tier and model
llm-apis.notes: Intended for prototyping, not production traffic. Rate limits are per-model.

llm-apis.name: Mistral La Plateforme (Experiment)
llm-apis.description: European-hosted Mistral family with a free Experiment mode worth roughly $10/month of credits, no card required.
llm-apis.free_limit: ~$10/month of credits in Experiment mode (about 1B tokens/month on small models)
llm-apis.notes: Experiment mode trains on your prompts by default. The 2 RPM limit makes it a batch/offline worker, not an interactive backend.

llm-apis.name: NVIDIA NIM API Catalog
llm-apis.description: Free hosted endpoints for NVIDIA-curated open models (Nemotron, Llama, DeepSeek), built for prototyping.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,000 API credits (26,000 total requests) on signup
llm-apis.notes: Credits are one-time and not refilled; some models are marked as evaluation-use only.

llm-apis.name: Z.ai GLM Flash Models
llm-apis.description: GLM-4.x Flash models served free of charge, popular as a drop-in for reasoning and coding agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unmetered access to GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash
llm-apis.notes: Flash tiers are free but rate-limited during peak hours in Asia.

llm-apis.name: Cohere Trial Keys
llm-apis.description: Every Cohere model including Command A and the Embed/Rerank family on a free trial key, non-commercial use only.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,000 API calls/month
llm-apis.notes: Trial keys explicitly prohibit production/commercial use — fine for a POC, not for a shipped product.

llm-apis.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
llm-apis.description: One router in front of 18 inference partners, with monthly free credits on any account.
llm-apis.free_limit: $0.10/month of included inference credits
llm-apis.notes: The $0.10/month allowance is genuinely small — treat this as a smoke-test credit, not a workload budget.

llm-apis.name: SambaNova Cloud
llm-apis.description: Very fast hosted open-model inference with a permanent per-model daily token allowance.
llm-apis.free_limit: 200,000 tokens/day per model
llm-apis.notes: Quota is per model, so stacking three models triples your effective daily allowance.

llm-apis.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio
llm-apis.description: Qwen family access with a free per-model token grant — the cleanest route to Qwen3 Coder for free.
llm-apis.free_limit: ~1M free tokens per model, valid 90 days
llm-apis.notes: Grants expire 90 days after activation and do not renew — good for a build sprint, not a standing tier.

llm-apis.name: Google Cloud Vertex AI Free Credits
llm-apis.description: Vertex AI access to Gemini and Model Garden on new-account credits — the enterprise-labelled alternative to AI Studio.
llm-apis.free_limit: $300 in new-customer credits valid 90 days
llm-apis.notes: Requires a billing account with a card, so it fails the strictest no-card filter — but the $300 covers a serious prototype.

llm-apis.name: Azure AI Foundry Free Credits
llm-apis.description: Azure-hosted OpenAI, Phi and Llama models with the new Azure free-account credit bundle.
llm-apis.free_limit: $200 in credits valid 30 days
llm-apis.notes: Identity verification with a card is mandatory; 30-day clock makes it a sprint budget.

llm-apis.name: Amazon Bedrock Free Tier
llm-apis.description: Bedrock-hosted Claude, Llama and Titan models on the AWS free tier for new accounts.
llm-apis.free_limit: Trial credits for Nova and select models for new AWS accounts
llm-apis.notes: Card required at signup. Bedrock model access must be requested per model in the console.

llm-apis.name: Baidu Qianfan (ERNIE)
llm-apis.description: ERNIE Speed and ERNIE Lite are permanently free on Baidu's Qianfan console for Chinese-language agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: ERNIE Speed and Lite free of charge; others on per-token billing
llm-apis.notes: Requires a mainland-China verified phone number for full access.

llm-apis.name: SiliconFlow
llm-apis.description: Chinese inference host that keeps a rotating set of open models free to call, including embedding and rerank models.
llm-apis.free_limit: Rotating set of free models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek small variants)
llm-apis.notes: Free model list changes without notice; the reranker and embedding models are the durable part.

llm-apis.name: Chutes.ai
llm-apis.description: Decentralised open-model inference with a community tier that costs nothing for low-volume agent calls.
llm-apis.free_limit: Community tier: quota-limited free requests across 100+ open models
llm-apis.notes: Community capacity is best-effort; expect queueing at peak. Fine for batch, risky for user-facing agents.

llm-apis.name: Vercel AI Gateway
llm-apis.description: One endpoint in front of every major provider with free monthly included credit and per-request observability.
llm-apis.free_limit: $5/month of included AI credits on the Hobby plan
llm-apis.notes: Also works as a BYOK proxy — you can route your existing free keys through it for logging and failover.

llm-apis.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
llm-apis.description: Free caching, rate-limiting and logging proxy placed in front of any provider, including your own free keys.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free on all plans; caching and analytics included
llm-apis.notes: The single highest-leverage free tool in this list: response caching can stretch a 1,000 req/day quota several-fold.

llm-apis.name: Fireworks AI
llm-apis.description: Fast open-model inference with a small no-card starter credit.
llm-apis.free_limit: $1 one-time credit
llm-apis.rate_limit: 10 RPM until a payment method is added
llm-apis.notes: The account suspends when the $1 is spent. Treat as a smoke test, not a tier.

llm-apis.name: Cerebras Cloud
llm-apis.description: Wafer-scale inference — still the fastest tokens/sec available — but the permanent free tier ended in July 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: $5 trial credit valid 30 days (card verification required since 2026-07-16)
llm-apis.notes: Downgraded from a no-card permanent free tier to a card-gated 30-day trial. Context is capped at 8K on trial.

llm-apis.name: DeepInfra
llm-apis.description: Cheap open-model inference with a small signup credit and no card requirement for the trial.
llm-apis.free_limit: $1.80 one-time credit

llm-apis.name: AI21 Studio
llm-apis.description: Jamba family models with a recurring free allowance aimed at evaluation.
llm-apis.free_limit: $10 in credits every 3 months on the free plan
llm-apis.notes: One of the few providers whose free credit refreshes on a schedule rather than once.

llm-apis.name: Moonshot Kimi API
llm-apis.description: Kimi K2 family with signup credit for long-context Chinese and English workloads.
llm-apis.free_limit: Signup trial credit (roughly ¥15)

llm-apis.name: ElevenLabs Free
llm-apis.description: Best-in-class TTS voices with a genuine monthly free character allowance, no card required.
llm-apis.free_limit: 10,000 characters/month
llm-apis.notes: Free-tier output requires attribution and cannot be used commercially.

llm-apis.name: Deepgram
llm-apis.description: Low-latency STT and TTS built for voice agents, with a large one-time credit and no card on signup.
llm-apis.free_limit: $200 one-time credit (roughly 100 hours of Nova-3 transcription)
llm-apis.notes: Credit is one-time; voice agents burn it fast. Pair with a local Whisper fallback.

llm-apis.name: AssemblyAI
llm-apis.description: Speech-to-text plus audio intelligence (summarisation, topic detection) on a no-card starter credit.
llm-apis.free_limit: $50 one-time credit plus rate-limited free transcription

llm-apis.name: Speechmatics
llm-apis.description: Accurate multilingual transcription with a recurring free monthly hour allowance.
llm-apis.free_limit: 8 hours of transcription/month

llm-apis.name: Google Cloud Speech & TTS
llm-apis.description: Production speech APIs with a standing free monthly allowance for STT and WaveNet/Neural2 voices.
llm-apis.free_limit: 60 min STT + 1M characters TTS per month
llm-apis.notes: The STT/TTS free allowance does not expire, unlike the $300 signup credit — this is one of the best long-term free voice stacks.

llm-apis.name: Azure AI Speech
llm-apis.description: Speech-to-text and neural TTS free allowances inside the Azure free account.
llm-apis.free_limit: 5 hours STT + 500K characters TTS per month

llm-apis.name: Stability AI
llm-apis.description: Stable Diffusion and Stable Audio via API, with a small recurring monthly credit grant.
llm-apis.free_limit: 25 credits/month on the free plan

llm-apis.name: Pollinations.AI
llm-apis.description: Completely keyless text and image generation API — the fastest possible zero-signup smoke test.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unmetered with fair-use rate limits; no API key at all
llm-apis.notes: No SLA and no guarantee of model availability — perfect for demos, unsuitable for production.

llm-apis.name: Leonardo.Ai API
llm-apis.description: Image generation API with a daily free token allowance tied to a free account.
llm-apis.free_limit: 150 free tokens/day (image generations)

llm-apis.name: Voyage AI
llm-apis.description: High-quality embeddings and rerankers with an unusually large free token grant for RAG prototypes.
llm-apis.free_limit: 200M free tokens across embedding and rerank models
llm-apis.notes: The 3 RPM limit is the real constraint — fine for indexing a corpus offline, painful for live retrieval.

llm-apis.name: Jina AI Embeddings & Reranker
llm-apis.description: Multilingual embeddings, reranker and reader APIs with a large free token allowance on one key.
llm-apis.free_limit: 10M free tokens on signup key

llm-apis.name: Mistral Codestral
llm-apis.description: Code-specialised completions and fill-in-the-middle model inside the Mistral free Experiment tier.
llm-apis.free_limit: Included in the Mistral free-tier monthly credit

llm-apis.name: Bhashini (ULCA)
llm-apis.description: India's national language platform — free STT, TTS, translation and OCR APIs for 22 scheduled languages.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for developers via the Bhashini API program
llm-apis.notes: Requires registration approval and a pipeline configuration — the signup is heavier than a typical vendor, but the API is genuinely free.

llm-apis.name: Sarvam AI
llm-apis.description: Indian-language LLMs (Sarvam-M), speech and translation APIs with signup credits for Indian developers.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free credits on signup; usage-based afterwards
llm-apis.notes: Indic-language models are the differentiator; English performance is below frontier tiers.

llm-apis.name: Ollama
llm-apis.description: The default way to run open models locally — one command to pull, serve and expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited; limited only by your GPU/RAM
llm-apis.notes: No rate limit and no data leaving your machine — the correct answer to 'what is the truly free LLM API'.

llm-apis.name: llama.cpp
llm-apis.description: Portable C/C++ inference engine that runs GGUF-quantised models on CPU, GPU or Apple Silicon.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT licensed)

llm-apis.name: LM Studio
llm-apis.description: Desktop GUI for local models with a one-click local server and built-in model discovery.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for personal and work use

llm-apis.name: vLLM
llm-apis.description: High-throughput serving engine with PagedAttention — the standard for self-hosted production inference.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, Apache 2.0)

llm-apis.name: Jan
llm-apis.description: Open-source offline ChatGPT alternative that can also expose a local OpenAI-compatible API.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, AGPL)

llm-apis.name: GPT4All
llm-apis.description: Consumer desktop app for running local models on modest hardware, with Python bindings for agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT)

llm-apis.name: MLX LM
llm-apis.description: Apple-silicon-optimised inference and fine-tuning library — the fastest local option on a Mac.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT)

llm-apis.name: LocalAI
llm-apis.description: Drop-in OpenAI API replacement that also speaks image, audio and embedding endpoints on modest hardware.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT)

llm-apis.name: KoboldCpp
llm-apis.description: Single-binary llama.cpp wrapper with a built-in web UI and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, AGPL)

llm-apis.name: llamafile
llm-apis.description: Single-file executable that bundles a model and a server — portable agent runtimes with zero install.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, Apache 2.0)

llm-apis.name: Text Generation WebUI
llm-apis.description: Feature-rich local web UI with OpenAI-compatible API, extensions and multi-model loading.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, AGPL)

llm-apis.name: faster-whisper
llm-apis.description: CTranslate2 reimplementation of Whisper that transcribes locally far faster than the reference build.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT)

llm-apis.name: Piper TTS
llm-apis.description: Fast, small neural TTS that runs on a Raspberry Pi — the free voice layer for offline agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, MIT)

llm-apis.name: Sentence Transformers
llm-apis.description: The standard library for local embeddings and reranking — 15K+ models, no API key, no quota.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, Apache 2.0)

llm-apis.name: FastEmbed
llm-apis.description: Lightweight ONNX embedding library — CPU-friendly local vectors that pair directly with Qdrant.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (self-hosted, Apache 2.0)

llm-apis.name: WebLLM
llm-apis.description: Runs quantised LLMs in the browser on WebGPU — zero server, zero cost, zero data egress.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (runs on the user's device)
llm-apis.notes: First load downloads 1-2GB of weights into the browser cache — design for that or you will lose users.

llm-apis.name: Transformers.js
llm-apis.description: Hugging Face pipelines running in the browser or Node via ONNX runtime, with WebGPU acceleration.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (runs locally/in-browser, Apache 2.0)

llm-apis.name: wllama
llm-apis.description: llama.cpp compiled to WebAssembly with WASM SIMD and threads — GGUF models straight in the browser.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited (client-side, MIT)

llm-apis.name: OpenAI API
llm-apis.description: No standing free tier. Data-sharing evaluation tokens are the only free path.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — no signup credits; $5 prepay minimum for API access
llm-apis.notes: Unless your org is eligible for the data-sharing token grant, treat OpenAI as paid-only.

llm-apis.name: Anthropic Claude API
llm-apis.description: No public free API tier; the OSS program grants Claude Max to qualifying maintainers instead.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — paid API only. OSS maintainer program gives a Claude Max seat
llm-apis.notes: Free chat on claude.ai is separate from API access — there is no free API key.

llm-apis.name: xAI Grok API
llm-apis.description: No documented free tier; console access requires prepaid credits.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — prepaid credits required

llm-apis.name: DeepSeek API
llm-apis.description: Extremely cheap per-token pricing, but no standing free tier and no signup grant since 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — top-up required (cheapest paid tokens on the market)
llm-apis.notes: DeepSeek weights are open — run V4-Flash locally for free rather than paying the API.

llm-apis.name: Together AI
llm-apis.description: 200+ open models, but the signup trial credit was retired; a $5 minimum purchase is required.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — $5 minimum purchase to start

llm-apis.name: Perplexity API (Sonar)
llm-apis.description: Search-grounded Sonar models are paid API only; the free consumer app is not API access.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — Pro subscribers get $5/month of API credit
llm-apis.notes: Tavily, Exa and Brave all have free search tiers — see the MCP list for agent-ready alternatives.

llm-apis.name: Dahl Inference
llm-apis.description: Anonymous open-model inference on a decentralised GPU network — 100M tokens per key with no account, no card and no signup, on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
llm-apis.free_limit: 100M tokens per API key
llm-apis.rate_limit: Not published; the 100M-token balance is the binding limit
llm-apis.notes: The 100M allowance is per key, not per day — issuance is unlimited, so you can mint another key when one is spent. Anonymous keys come from POST /tokens. Direct curl calls frequently trip a Cloudflare challenge (403); the browser chat and the documented endpoints work. Runs on the Gonka compute network.

llm-apis.name: LLM7.io
llm-apis.description: Gateway you can call with the literal placeholder key "unused" — no account, no email, no card, just a base URL and an OpenAI SDK.
llm-apis.free_limit: 10 req/min anonymous; 40 req/min with a free token
llm-apis.notes: The widely-repeated "2 req/s, 20 RPM, 100 req/hr" figures do not match the vendor documentation: anonymous access is 10 req/min and a free token from token.llm7.io raises it to 40 req/min. Anonymous traffic only reaches the turbo model set.

llm-apis.name: OVHcloud AI Endpoints
llm-apis.description: EU-hosted, GDPR-friendly inference over 20+ open-weight models at $0, usable without an API key on the anonymous tier.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free — $0 per request on the anonymous tier
llm-apis.notes: The API host is oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net — posting to the marketing domain returns 405. Anonymous calls are accepted and then answered with "API rate limit exceeded", which is how the ~2 req/min cap presents itself; no key is required to reach that point. The published catalogue returns pricing of 0 for prompt, completion and request.

llm-apis.name: Hack Club AI
llm-apis.description: Free OpenAI-compatible access to Gemini, GPT-5.2, Kimi K2 and 30+ other models for Hack Clubbers — the most generous free tier aimed at teenage developers.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for Hack Club members
llm-apis.notes: Gated on a Hack Club account, which is aimed at students and teenage hackers. Not a general-purpose public tier — do not list it as one.

llm-apis.name: Space Bunny Alpha
llm-apis.description: Anonymous stealth model on OpenRouter with a 1M-token context window, free at $0 in and $0 out while the provider stays cloaked.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free ($0/$0 per million tokens) while the preview runs
llm-apis.notes: Confirmed live against OpenRouter's model API on 2026-09-24. Stealth previews are temporary by design: Ox Alpha, the previous drop, was unmasked as Z.AI's GLM-5.3-Flash and removed from the free catalogue within a week — which is exactly why it is not listed here. Needs an OpenRouter account, and prompts are handled by an anonymous provider, so keep secrets out of it.

llm-apis.name: ZenMux
llm-apis.description: Unified gateway over 100+ models that keeps a small set of model ids permanently free, including DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision and GLM-5.3.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free model ids, including deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp-free and z-ai/glm-5.3-free
llm-apis.notes: The gateway as a whole is commercial — only the -free suffixed model ids cost nothing. Paid tiers advertise a 5% service-fee discount on top-up, so expect upsell copy on the pricing page.

llm-apis.name: Puter.js
llm-apis.description: Client-side JavaScript SDK that gives a web app AI, storage, database and auth with no backend — the developer pays nothing because each signed-in user spends credits from their own Puter account.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for developers; end users spend their own Puter credits
llm-apis.notes: Usually marketed as "free and unlimited", which is only half true. It is genuinely free for the developer, but not unlimited: once a user exhausts their Puter allocation they pay Puter directly, so an app with heavy anonymous traffic will hit a wall. The open-source developer tools that wrap it as a drop-in OpenAI server are unmaintained third-party bridges and are not listed.

mcp-servers.name: Filesystem
mcp-servers.description: Secure local file operations with configurable allow-listed directories — the reference server every local agent starts with.
mcp-servers.notes: Always pass an explicit allow-listed root. Running it on `/` gives an agent write access to your whole machine.

mcp-servers.name: Fetch
mcp-servers.description: Fetches a URL and converts it to clean markdown for the model, with robots.txt respect and chunked reading.

mcp-servers.name: Git
mcp-servers.description: Read, search and diff a local git repository — history-aware agents without shelling out to raw git.

mcp-servers.name: Memory (Knowledge Graph)
mcp-servers.description: Persistent knowledge-graph memory stored as local JSON — gives an agent recall across sessions for free.
mcp-servers.notes: Pair with a free vector store (Qdrant or Chroma) when the graph grows past a few thousand entities.

mcp-servers.name: Sequential Thinking
mcp-servers.description: Structured step-by-step reasoning with revision and branching — measurably improves multi-step agent plans.

mcp-servers.name: Time
mcp-servers.description: Time and timezone conversion grounded in the host clock — stops agents hallucinating dates.

mcp-servers.name: Everything (Test Server)
mcp-servers.description: Reference server exercising every MCP primitive — the fastest way to test a new client or transport.

mcp-servers.name: GitHub MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Repo automation, PRs, issues, code search and CI workflows — the most-starred MCP server in the ecosystem.
mcp-servers.notes: A hosted remote variant is available at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ if you would rather not run Docker.

mcp-servers.name: Playwright MCP
mcp-servers.description: Browser automation over accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots — deterministic agent browsing in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
mcp-servers.notes: Accessibility-tree snapshots use far fewer tokens than screenshot-based browser agents.

mcp-servers.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
mcp-servers.description: Drives a real Chrome instance for performance traces, console errors and network inspection.

mcp-servers.name: Notion MCP
mcp-servers.description: Reads and writes Notion pages and databases — the cleanest way to give an agent a knowledge base you already maintain.
mcp-servers.notes: Remember to share the specific pages with the integration — a token alone grants nothing.

mcp-servers.name: Sentry MCP
mcp-servers.description: Pulls issues, stack traces and traces into the prompt so an agent can triage production errors.

mcp-servers.name: Supabase MCP
mcp-servers.description: Postgres schema, migrations, edge functions and logs through one authenticated server.
mcp-servers.notes: Start with --read-only; agents granted DDL rights will eventually drop something you wanted.

mcp-servers.name: MongoDB MCP
mcp-servers.description: Query, aggregate and inspect collections, including Atlas administration.

mcp-servers.name: Redis MCP
mcp-servers.description: Key-value access, data structure operations and vector set queries against Redis or Upstash.

mcp-servers.name: Cloudflare MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Fifteen-plus specialised servers for Workers, R2, D1, DNS, logs and Workers AI.
mcp-servers.notes: Each Cloudflare product ships its own server; pick the observability or bindings one rather than enabling all of them.

mcp-servers.name: Vercel MCP
mcp-servers.description: Deployments, build logs, environment variables and project configuration.

mcp-servers.name: AWS MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Official suite covering S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudWatch and 20+ other services.
mcp-servers.notes: Scope IAM to a read-only role before letting an agent near your account.

mcp-servers.name: Azure MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Natural-language management of Azure resources with Entra ID authentication.

mcp-servers.name: Google Cloud MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Managed MCP endpoints for Cloud Run, BigQuery, Spanner and gcloud workflows.
mcp-servers.notes: Google has renamed and reorganised these packages several times in 2026 — confirm the current package name on the docs page before copying the install line.

mcp-servers.name: Docker MCP Gateway
mcp-servers.description: Container management plus a gateway that catalogs and proxies hundreds of other MCP servers.

mcp-servers.name: Kubernetes MCP
mcp-servers.description: kubectl-style cluster operations — inspect pods, apply manifests and read logs.
mcp-servers.notes: Point it at a non-production context. An agent with cluster-admin is a very efficient way to delete a namespace.

mcp-servers.name: Terraform MCP
mcp-servers.description: Provider and module registry lookups plus plan/apply assistance for infrastructure as code.

mcp-servers.name: Grafana MCP
mcp-servers.description: Query dashboards, Loki logs and Prometheus metrics from inside the agent loop.

mcp-servers.name: Elasticsearch MCP
mcp-servers.description: Search indices and run aggregations; works against Elastic Cloud or self-hosted.

mcp-servers.name: Stripe MCP
mcp-servers.description: Read customers, invoices and subscriptions, and create payment links from a prompt.
mcp-servers.notes: Use a restricted key in test mode. --tools=all grants write access to live objects if the key allows it.

mcp-servers.name: Framelink Figma MCP
mcp-servers.description: Pulls design tokens, layout and component structure out of Figma files into the editor, over stdio, using a personal access token.
notes: Renamed from 'Figma MCP' to name its maintainer: this is the community Framelink server, not Figma's own. For the first-party server see figma-mcp-server.
Works over stdio with a personal access token, so it needs no OAuth dance and no Figma desktop app — which is why people still reach for it over the official remote server.

mcp-servers.name: Linear MCP
mcp-servers.description: Create, search and update issues and projects in Linear from the agent loop.

mcp-servers.name: Atlassian MCP
mcp-servers.description: Jira issues and Confluence pages — the enterprise ticketing counterpart to Linear.

mcp-servers.name: Zapier MCP

mcp-servers.name: Browserbase MCP

mcp-servers.name: Chroma MCP

mcp-servers.name: SQLite MCP

mcp-servers.name: MySQL MCP Server

mcp-servers.name: Context7

mcp-servers.name: Firecrawl MCP

mcp-servers.name: Exa MCP

mcp-servers.name: Tavily MCP
mcp-servers.description: Search, extract and map endpoints purpose-built for LLM grounding, with a genuinely usable free tier.

mcp-servers.name: Brave Search MCP

mcp-servers.name: DeepWiki MCP

mcp-servers.name: Ref MCP

mcp-servers.name: Wikipedia MCP

mcp-servers.name: Obsidian MCP

mcp-servers.name: FastMCP

mcp-servers.name: OpenAPI MCP Server

mcp-servers.name: AntV Chart MCP

mcp-servers.name: Google Drive (Archived)

mcp-servers.name: Brave Search (Archived Reference)

mcp-servers.name: Wikidata MCP
mcp-servers.description: Semantic and keyword search over Wikidata's ~30M entities and properties, so agents can resolve vague concepts into verifiable QIDs before writing SPARQL.
mcp-servers.notes: Hosted as a public instance by Wikimedia Deutschland, so there is nothing to install or pay for. Exposes vector_search_items, keyword_search_items and vector_search_properties. Endpoint rejects plain GETs (406) by design — point an MCP client at it rather than curl.

mcp-servers.name: Figma MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Figma's own MCP server, hosted at mcp.figma.com over Streamable HTTP. Reads a selected frame's variables, components and layout into the editor, generates code from it, reuses real components through Code Connect and, while in beta, writes native content back to the canvas.
mcp-servers.install: claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp
notes: A hosted remote server rather than a package: https://mcp.figma.com/mcp answers 401 without a token, so there is nothing to install — you add the URL and authenticate.

Free to connect on Figma's free Starter plan, but that plan and View or Collab seats on paid plans are capped at 6 tool calls per month. Dev and Full seats on paid plans get Tier 1 REST API limits instead. This is a real free allowance, not a generous one — the Studio plan at $16/month is what most people will need for daily use.
Writing to the canvas is free during the beta, and Figma has said it will become a usage-based paid feature. Assume it will not stay free.
Also installable as Claude Code and Cursor plugins and as a Gemini CLI extension, which bundle the server config together with the Figma skill pack below.

agent-tools.free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

Often quoted as "100% on benchmarks" — that is the hybrid pipeline with cloud reranking, which the authors themselves flagged as tuned on failing questions. The defensible numbers are 96.6% R@5 raw on LongMemEval with zero API calls and a 98.4% held-out hybrid score.
The project publicly walked back an overstated "30x lossless compression" claim; its experimental AAAK mode actually regresses to 84.2%.

agent-tools.name: Cognee
agent-tools.description: Open-source memory platform that builds a self-hosted knowledge graph from your data, giving agents persistent long-term memory across sessions.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — self-hosted, runs with local extraction and embedding models
agent-tools.notes: Runs end to end without an OpenAI or Anthropic key by using local extraction and embedding models, which is unusual for knowledge-graph memory. A hosted tier exists for teams that would rather not self-host.

agent-tools.name: Mem0
agent-tools.description: Drop-in memory layer for agents that extracts and stores salient facts between sessions, with the widest framework support of any memory library.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free open-source self-host; hosted tier includes 10K memories
agent-tools.notes: The most-starred memory project by a wide margin. Extraction-based like its benchmarks measure against — it summarises rather than storing verbatim, so recall depends on the extraction step. The hosted platform is a paid product beyond the free allowance.

agent-tools.name: Nanobrowser
agent-tools.description: Open-source Chrome extension that runs multi-agent web workflows — extract, compare and fill forms — inside your own browser, on your own keys.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0 extension, works with any provider including Ollama and Groq
agent-tools.notes: The pitch is "open-source alternative to OpenAI Operator", and its real advantage is BYOK: pair it with Ollama for a fully local browser agent, or with a free Groq/Gemini key. Chrome-family browsers only.

agent-tools.name: Freebuff
agent-tools.description: Coding agent funded by terminal advertising — desktop, CLI, web and chat clients all backed by frontier models at no cost, in exchange for text ads.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free with ad support; no subscription
agent-tools.notes: Marked degraded rather than active because the business model is the product: the vendor sells terminal ad impressions to fund inference, so model access and the ad load can both change without notice. Closed source, and the "unlimited" wording is marketing — throughput is throttled in practice. Do not point anything production-critical at it.

agent-tools.name: KISS Sorcar
agent-tools.description: Local-first agent framework that runs as a VS Code extension plus web and mobile clients, routing to any of hundreds of models across nine provider categories.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free framework (Apache-2.0) — pay only your model provider
agent-tools.notes: The "KISS" in the name is the design brief. Provider counts and third-party agent integrations move quickly in this project, so treat any specific number (661 models, 43 agents) as a snapshot rather than a spec.

agent-tools.name: ReadyAgents Core
agent-tools.description: Self-hosted workflow engine and MCP toolkit that records agent runs so you can replay them offline, fork a run, diff two runs, or freeze one into a regression test.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — self-hosted, bring your own provider keys
agent-tools.notes: The record/replay/diff loop is the genuinely unusual part — most agent frameworks still have no first-class way to turn a production run into a regression test.

agent-tools.name: NanoBot
agent-tools.description: Deliberately tiny personal-agent framework from the HKU Data Intelligence lab that reimplements most of a large agent stack in roughly 4K lines.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, bring your own provider keys
agent-tools.notes: Actively developed by a research lab and worth reading end-to-end precisely because it is small. The "90% of OpenClaw's capabilities" figure is the project's own framing, not a measured comparison.

agent-tools.name: Pincer
agent-tools.description: Self-hosted personal agent that lives in your messaging apps — WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal and email — with a large native tool set plus everything reachable over MCP.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — self-hosted via Docker, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: Skill signing and audit logs are the differentiators: an agent wired into your WhatsApp can take real actions on your behalf, so its security posture matters more than a coding agent's.

agent-tools.name: QwenPaw
agent-tools.description: Personal assistant agent that runs fully locally against its own bundled QwenPaw-Flash models, so it needs no API key and no cloud account at all.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — local models included (2B/4B/9B)
agent-tools.notes: Genuinely key-free out of the box rather than BYOK, which is rare. Connectors skew to Chinese platforms (DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, QQ) alongside Discord, Telegram and iMessage. A 2B-9B local model is a capable assistant, not a frontier-reasoning substitute.

agent-tools.name: Tares
agent-tools.description: Self-hostable data plane for always-on agents: ingest events from Prometheus, OpenTelemetry and webhooks, then let an MCP server act on them.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, runs on your own machine
agent-tools.notes: Targets the gap between "an agent that answers" and one that reacts to what your infrastructure is actually doing.

agent-tools.name: Kitaru
agent-tools.description: Durable-execution runtime for Python agents from the ZenML team: record, replay and improve agent runs in production.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, self-hosted
agent-tools.notes: Submitted as "ZenML/Kitaru"; the canonical repository is zenml-io/kitaru. Built by the team behind ZenML, which is the main reason to trust it at this age.

agent-tools.name: Nexora
agent-tools.description: Self-hosted orchestration platform where agents get personas, skills and tools, with sub-agent delegation, RAG and semantic memory.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed self-hosted core
agent-tools.notes: Early-stage (tens of stars, commits this month). Useful if you want a self-hosted multi-agent UI today; audit it before pointing it at anything sensitive.

agent-tools.name: Automatos AI
agent-tools.description: Apache-2.0 multi-agent orchestration platform built around RAG and vector embeddings, able to route through free provider tiers including NVIDIA's.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: Judge it as a multi-agent orchestration stack; the "neural field theory" framing is not an evaluable claim.

agent-tools.name: aigate
agent-tools.description: Single-compose self-hosted AI platform bundling inference, tool use, browser automation, image generation, speech synthesis, transcription and object storage.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — self-hosted; bundled providers have their own free tiers
agent-tools.notes: Small project with a wide attack surface — one compose file exposing inference, storage and code execution. Read the compose file before exposing it beyond localhost.

agent-tools.name: miii-cli
agent-tools.description: Offline coding agent for the terminal that runs entirely on Ollama, positioned as a local alternative to Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free forever — MIT licensed, no keys, no cloud
agent-tools.notes: Small but actively developed. Output quality tracks whichever local model you point it at, so pair it with a decent coding model rather than a 3B.

agent-tools.name: PawWork
agent-tools.description: Desktop agent for macOS and Windows with free models bundled in, aimed at office files, web search and scheduled automations rather than code.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, bundled models need no API key
agent-tools.notes: The no-key, no-terminal framing makes it a genuine on-ramp for non-developers. Bundled free models change without notice, since they depend on upstream providers.

agent-tools.name: Code Buddy
agent-tools.description: Local-first coding agent that reads your repo, writes code and runs commands, with terminal, HTTP and optional desktop interfaces plus fleet collaboration.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — runs at $0 with Ollama; optional ChatGPT subscription integration
agent-tools.notes: The Ollama path is the supported free route and is why this is listed. Its optional ChatGPT-subscription mode routes through a consumer account rather than an API, which is outside that provider's terms — use the local path.

agent-tools.name: BrowserOS
agent-tools.description: Open-source agentic browser — a Chromium-based alternative to ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity Comet and Dia, with agents built into the browser rather than bolted on.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — AGPL-3.0, bring your own model keys
agent-tools.notes: The submission pointed at a one-star fork (gHashTag/BrowserOS); this is the upstream project. AGPL-3.0 matters if you plan to redistribute a modified build.

agent-tools.name: UI-TARS Desktop
agent-tools.description: ByteDance's multimodal GUI agent stack that drives a real desktop — clicking, typing and navigating native apps — from screenshots and instructions.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, run the model locally or bring a key
agent-tools.notes: One of the few computer-use stacks with real industrial backing and a permissive licence. A GUI agent that can click anything on your screen is a large security decision — run it in a VM or on a spare machine.

agent-tools.name: Open Cowork
agent-tools.description: Desktop agent for Windows and macOS that installs Claude Code and MCP tooling in one click and runs the agent in a sandbox.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: Sandbox isolation is the feature that matters here — the whole point of this class of tool is letting an agent act on your machine, and the sandbox is what bounds the blast radius.

agent-tools.name: Abu-Cowork
agent-tools.description: Local-first desktop agent with self-evolving skills and multi-model support, built as a privacy-preserving alternative to hosted coworking agents.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: Mid-sized community project. "Self-evolving skills" means it writes new skills for itself over time — keep an eye on what it accumulates.

agent-tools.name: HyperDesk
agent-tools.description: Desktop coding workbench where the agent reads the project, runs commands, drives a browser and coordinates subagents — asking before it changes anything.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: The confirm-before-changing behaviour is the right default for a tool with this much reach. Young project — check the package's own release notes before trusting it with a large repo.

agent-tools.name: Alice Memory
agent-tools.description: Local-first continuity layer that lets agents resume interrupted work, track open loops and recall decisions with provenance, exposed over MCP, HTTP and CLI.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, local, no API keys
agent-tools.notes: Provenance — remembering why a decision was made, not just what it was — is the part most memory layers skip. The 79.4% LongMemEval figure is the project's own reported number, not independently reproduced here.

agent-tools.name: Mazu
agent-tools.description: Coding-agent CLI with a memory and checkpoint layer: it keeps a queryable record of project decisions, conventions and past mistakes across sessions.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
agent-tools.notes: Pair it with any of the free coding models catalogued here. As with every local memory store, the retrieval quality matters more than the storage format.

agent-tools.name: pi-coding-agent
agent-tools.description: Minimal, inspectable coding agent that persists project facts to a plain .pi/memory.md file instead of a hidden database, with self-review and autonomous tool use.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, multi-provider
agent-tools.notes: Storing memory as readable Markdown you can edit and review is the whole appeal — no opaque vector store to debug when recall goes wrong.

agent-tools.name: mengram-ai
agent-tools.description: Human-like memory layer for agents with auto-save, auto-recall and a cognitive profile, split across semantic, episodic and procedural memory and exposed as MCP tools.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, runs locally
agent-tools.notes: Splitting memory into semantic, episodic and procedural stores is a more honest model of how agents actually benefit from memory than a single flat vector index. Actively released and includes Claude Code hooks.

agent-tools.name: haiku.rag
agent-tools.description: Agentic RAG that runs locally by default, using Ollama-hosted open models for the full pipeline — ingestion, embeddings, retrieval and generation.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source; the default pipeline needs no external API key
agent-tools.notes: Scales from a laptop to a server without changing the stack, and the no-key default is the reason it belongs in this catalogue rather than in a generic RAG list.

agent-tools.name: Pinakes
agent-tools.description: Portable, agent-first knowledge base where one directory holds the corpus, retrieved with SQLite FTS5 lexical search plus local embeddings and local reranking.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — no API key needed to search or re-index
agent-tools.notes: Combining BM25 with embeddings is more robust than either alone — lexical search catches exact identifiers that pure vector search misses, and re-indexing costs nothing.

agent-tools.name: Arc Rector
agent-tools.description: Agentic RAG stack assembled entirely from open-source components, with nine swappable layers so you can replace any piece without touching the rest.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, no API keys, no vendor bills
agent-tools.notes: Worth reading as a reference architecture even if you do not adopt it — the swappable-layer structure is a clean answer to RAG stacks that hard-code one vendor.

agent-tools.name: local-rag-assistant
agent-tools.description: Chat with any codebase locally: AST-aware chunking, Ollama embeddings and a Chroma vector store, with no code leaving your machine.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — fully local, no API keys
agent-tools.notes: AST-aware chunking beats naive line splitting on code, because a function is the unit you actually want retrieved. Small community project — read before you run.

agent-tools.name: Pleias SLM RAG
agent-tools.description: On-device RAG API built on a ~300M-parameter model small enough to run on a Raspberry Pi 5, with no GPU and no external API calls.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0 model weights
agent-tools.notes: Genuinely edge-sized, which is rare for anything labelled RAG. A 300M model is for retrieval and grounded short answers, not general reasoning.

agent-tools.name: HOL Guard
agent-tools.description: Antivirus and runtime protection layer for agent tooling — plugins, skills and MCP servers — that sits between your agent and the code it is about to run.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — runs locally, no account
agent-tools.notes: Installing an MCP server means running someone else's code with your credentials in reach; this is one of the few tools treating that as the security boundary it is. Integrates with the major agent CLIs.

agent-tools.name: agent-bom
agent-tools.description: Scanner and self-hosted control plane for AI infrastructure — sweeps agent configs, MCP servers, instruction files, containers, cloud estate and model artefacts.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
agent-tools.notes: The agent-specific targets — instruction files and MCP configs — are what distinguish it from a generic container scanner. Actively released.

agent-tools.name: PanGuard
agent-tools.description: One-command monitoring and guarding for agents and MCP servers, aimed at catching what an agent does rather than what it was asked to do.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, 100% open source
agent-tools.notes: Deliberately low-friction — one command and it starts watching, which is the right trade for teams that will not stand up a full security stack.

agent-tools.name: Bawbel Scanner
agent-tools.description: Security scanner for MCP servers and AI skill files that scores findings against OWASP's AIVSS rubric and ships an open vulnerability database with a public API.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source
agent-tools.notes: Scoring MCP servers against a published rubric is useful because it makes two servers comparable. AIVSS is still evolving, so treat scores as guidance rather than verdicts.

agent-tools.name: Nightona
agent-tools.description: Community continuation of Daytona: elastic sandbox infrastructure for running AI-generated code and agent workflows in isolation.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — AGPL-3.0, self-hosted
agent-tools.notes: Forked from Daytona's last AGPL-3.0 release after that project changed direction, so the licence is what makes the continuation legitimate — and it means you inherit the maintenance burden rather than a vendor's.

agent-tools.name: Capka
agent-tools.description: Self-hosted sandbox for AI agents, built as a community alternative to hosted coworking sandboxes.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
agent-tools.notes: Young project — verify the isolation boundary yourself before trusting it with untrusted code, since that is precisely the promise being made.

agent-tools.name: coder-eval
agent-tools.description: Agent-agnostic framework for evaluating and benchmarking coding agents and skills, with support for comparing different agent harnesses head to head.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source
agent-tools.notes: Agent-agnostic is the valuable property: you can A/B your own agent against a reference harness instead of trusting a vendor's self-reported score.

agent-tools.name: OpenMCP
agent-tools.description: Self-hosted benchmarking harness for computer-use agents acting through MCP, letting you measure tool-using agents reproducibly.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
agent-tools.notes: Computer-use evaluation is the least standardised corner of agent testing, so any harness that makes results reproducible is worth knowing about. Early-stage project.

agent-tools.name: agent-eval
agent-tools.description: Evaluation framework that auto-generates test tasks for an agent, executes them and scores results across several dimensions.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — open source
agent-tools.notes: Auto-generated tasks solve the blank-page problem in agent testing, but they measure what the generator thought to ask — combine with your own regression cases.

agent-tools.name: BenchClaw
agent-tools.description: Multi-dimensional agent evaluation that scores runs across ten dimensions and visualises the spread as radar charts.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free — MIT licensed
agent-tools.notes: Multi-dimensional scoring is more informative than a single pass/fail number. The advertised "17-judge AI tribunal" and deception detection are separate LLM calls judging output — treat their verdicts as signal, not ground truth.

free-tiers.name: Vercel
free-tiers.description: Static and serverless hosting with preview deployments per branch and AI Gateway included.
free-tiers.notes: Hobby is explicitly non-commercial. Fine for a side project, against ToS for a paid product.

free-tiers.name: Netlify
free-tiers.description: Static hosting, edge functions and form handling with per-branch deploy previews.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare Pages
free-tiers.description: Unlimited-bandwidth static hosting that pairs with Workers, D1 and R2 on the same free account.
free-tiers.notes: The best free host for this site's own architecture: static output, no egress billing, global CDN.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare Workers
free-tiers.description: V8-isolate serverless functions with cron triggers and durable objects, plus a free Workers AI binding.
free-tiers.notes: The free tier's 10ms CPU limit is generous for API orchestration and tight for anything doing real compute.

free-tiers.name: GitHub Pages
free-tiers.description: Static hosting straight from a repository, with a custom domain and HTTPS included.

free-tiers.name: Render
free-tiers.description: Container and web-service hosting with managed Postgres and cron jobs.
free-tiers.free_limit: 750 instance-hours/mo; services spin down after 15 min idle
free-tiers.notes: The 15-minute spin-down makes cold starts of 30-60s. Fine for demos, painful for a live agent endpoint.

free-tiers.name: Railway
free-tiers.description: Fast deploys from a repo or Dockerfile with databases attached, billed by usage.
free-tiers.free_limit: Trial credits on signup; $5/mo Hobby credit afterwards

free-tiers.name: Fly.io
free-tiers.description: Runs Docker containers close to users with persistent volumes and private networking.
free-tiers.free_limit: Limited free VM allowance for small machines (no managed databases)

free-tiers.name: Koyeb
free-tiers.description: Serverless container platform with a small always-on free instance and GPU options.
free-tiers.free_limit: One free web service instance (0.1 vCPU / 512MB)

free-tiers.name: Deno Deploy
free-tiers.description: Edge TypeScript runtime with KV storage, queues and cron built in — no build step.

free-tiers.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
free-tiers.description: The only genuinely free-forever VPS with usable specs — 2 Arm Ampere cores and 12GB RAM running 24/7, as one VM or split in two.
free-tiers.free_limit: 2 ARM OCPUs + 12GB RAM, 200GB storage, 10TB egress/mo, forever
notes: Oracle halved this allowance on 15 June 2026 — 4 OCPU/24GB became 2 OCPU/12GB — with no announcement, only a quiet docs edit.
Instances above the new limit were terminated after 18 August 2026.
The pool is tenancy-wide, not per-instance.
Idle instances are reclaimed: under 20% 95th-percentile CPU, network and memory across a seven-day window.
Signup rejections are routine, and ARM capacity is scarce enough that launches frequently fail with "Out of capacity"; Pay As You Go accounts reportedly keep the old 4/24 allowance for free.

free-tiers.name: AWS Free Tier
free-tiers.description: Twelve months of t4g.small, Lambda allowances and 5GB S3, plus always-free Lambda and DynamoDB caps.
free-tiers.free_limit: 12-month credits for new accounts; perpetual Lambda/DynamoDB allowances

free-tiers.name: Google Cloud Free Tier
free-tiers.description: e2-micro VM, Cloud Run and Firestore allowances, plus the $300 new-account credit.
free-tiers.free_limit: Always-free e2-micro VM + Cloud Run/Speech/BigQuery monthly quotas

free-tiers.name: Hugging Face Spaces
free-tiers.description: Free Docker or Gradio container hosting with a permanent public URL — 2 vCPU and 16GB RAM on the CPU Basic tier, enough for a real service rather than a toy demo.
free-tiers.free_limit: 2 vCPU / 16GB RAM / 50GB ephemeral disk, unlimited Spaces
notes: One of the most generous free CPU containers available, and it needs no card at any point.
Spaces sleep after inactivity and cold-start on the next visit, so this is not an always-on host without a keep-alive.
The 50GB disk is ephemeral and resets on every restart; persistent /data storage is a paid upgrade from $5/mo for 20GB. Back state up to a Storage Bucket or dataset repo instead.
Private Spaces are restricted on the free tier, so treat a free Space as public.

free-tiers.name: Google Colab
free-tiers.description: Free hosted Jupyter with a T4 GPU — the cheapest path to fine-tuning or running a large model.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free GPU sessions (T4), subject to availability and session limits
free-tiers.notes: Free GPU availability is not guaranteed at peak times and sessions die after idle periods — not a deploy target.

free-tiers.name: Kaggle Notebooks
free-tiers.description: Free GPU/TPU notebooks with 30 hours of weekly GPU quota and persistent datasets.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30 GPU hours/week (P100 or T4x2), 20 TPU hours/week

free-tiers.name: Modal
free-tiers.description: Serverless Python with GPU-per-second billing — good for embedding jobs and batch inference.
free-tiers.free_limit: $30/month of included compute on the free plan
free-tiers.notes: $30/month covers a lot of embedding generation; it does not cover sustained GPU inference.

free-tiers.name: E2B
free-tiers.description: Sandboxed cloud VMs built for agent code execution, with filesystem and process control.

free-tiers.name: Val Town
free-tiers.description: Write and deploy TypeScript functions in the browser with cron, SQLite and secrets included.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free tier with 100K daily function runs

free-tiers.name: Supabase
free-tiers.description: Postgres with auth, storage, realtime and pgvector in one free project — the default agent backend.
free-tiers.notes: Free projects pause after 7 days of inactivity. Set up a weekly keep-alive ping or accept the cold start.

free-tiers.name: Neon
free-tiers.description: Serverless Postgres with copy-on-write branching — a database branch per feature or per agent run.

free-tiers.name: Turso
free-tiers.description: Edge SQLite with embedded replicas — sub-millisecond reads next to your function, plus native vector search.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare D1
free-tiers.description: SQLite at the edge, bound directly to Workers with no connection pooling to manage.

free-tiers.name: CockroachDB Basic
free-tiers.description: Distributed SQL with automatic replication across regions and standard Postgres wire protocol.

free-tiers.name: MongoDB Atlas
free-tiers.description: Managed document database with a permanent M0 cluster, including Atlas Vector Search.
free-tiers.notes: Card verification is required even for M0 in most regions now — the one free database that usually asks.

free-tiers.name: Firebase Firestore
free-tiers.description: Realtime document database with offline sync and client SDKs for every platform.

free-tiers.name: Aiven
free-tiers.description: Managed Postgres, MySQL, Valkey and OpenSearch on a single always-free plan.
free-tiers.free_limit: One 1GB managed service (Postgres, MySQL, Valkey or OpenSearch)

free-tiers.name: Convex
free-tiers.description: Reactive backend with TypeScript queries, mutations, scheduled functions and vector search.

free-tiers.name: Upstash Redis
free-tiers.description: Serverless Redis with per-request pricing and a REST API — no connection limit problems from serverless functions.

free-tiers.name: PocketBase
free-tiers.description: Single-binary backend with SQLite, auth, file storage, realtime and an admin UI — self-host anywhere.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare R2
free-tiers.description: S3-compatible object storage with zero egress fees — the reason to store agent artefacts here.
free-tiers.free_limit: 10GB storage, 1M Class A ops/mo, free egress

free-tiers.name: Backblaze B2
free-tiers.description: Cheap S3-compatible object storage with free egress through Cloudflare's bandwidth alliance.

free-tiers.name: Qdrant Cloud
free-tiers.description: The best free vector tier: a real cluster with payload filtering, no card required.
free-tiers.free_limit: 1GB cluster free forever (0.5 vCPU, 1GB RAM, 4GB disk)
free-tiers.notes: 1GB holds roughly 250K vectors at 384 dimensions — enough for a serious RAG prototype.

free-tiers.name: Pinecone Starter
free-tiers.description: Fully managed vector database with the least operational overhead of any option here.
free-tiers.free_limit: 2GB storage, 2M write units and 1M read units/mo, 5 indexes
free-tiers.notes: Free indexes are pinned to AWS us-east-1 — latency from India or Europe is noticeable.

free-tiers.name: Weaviate Cloud
free-tiers.description: Open-source vector database with hybrid keyword+vector search and built-in vectoriser modules.

free-tiers.name: Zilliz Cloud
free-tiers.description: Managed Milvus with strong performance at scale and a genuine free cluster.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free tier: 5GB storage, 2.5M vector compute units/mo

free-tiers.name: Upstash Vector
free-tiers.description: Serverless vector database over REST — no connection management, pairs with Upstash Redis on one key.

free-tiers.name: Chroma Cloud
free-tiers.description: Managed version of the most developer-friendly embedded vector store, with $5 of starter credit.
free-tiers.free_limit: $5 starter credit; Chroma OSS remains free to self-host
free-tiers.notes: For anything under a few hundred thousand vectors, self-hosted Chroma on the same box as your app is simpler and free.

free-tiers.name: Neo4j AuraDB Free
free-tiers.description: Managed graph database with native vector indexes — a knowledge graph and a vector store in one.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free instance: 200K nodes, 400K relationships, no card required

free-tiers.name: pgvector
free-tiers.description: Postgres extension that turns the database you already run into a vector store — no second system to operate.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (extension; self-hosted or on any Postgres free tier)
free-tiers.notes: Available out of the box on Supabase and Neon free tiers — the pragmatic default for a small agent.

free-tiers.name: LanceDB
free-tiers.description: Embedded vector database on the Lance columnar format — runs in-process, no server, no account.

free-tiers.name: Clerk
free-tiers.description: Drop-in authentication with prebuilt UI components, organisations and webhooks.

free-tiers.name: WorkOS AuthKit
free-tiers.description: Auth with enterprise SSO, SCIM and directory sync built in from day one.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free up to 1M monthly active users on AuthKit
free-tiers.notes: The 1M MAU number makes this the strongest free option if you might later need enterprise SSO.

free-tiers.name: Auth0
free-tiers.description: Mature identity platform with social logins, MFA and rules/extensibility.

free-tiers.name: Logto
free-tiers.description: Open-source auth alternative to Auth0 with a clean developer experience and a free cloud tier.
free-tiers.free_limit: 50,000 MAU on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited

free-tiers.name: Better Auth
free-tiers.description: TypeScript-first authentication library that lives inside your app — no third party in the request path.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (MIT, self-hosted in your own codebase)
free-tiers.notes: For an agent app, a library beats a hosted auth service: no MAU cliff, no extra vendor.

free-tiers.name: Keycloak
free-tiers.description: Red Hat's battle-tested identity server — full OIDC/SAML with self-hosting on a free VM.

free-tiers.name: Upstash QStash
free-tiers.description: HTTP-based message queue and scheduler — the simplest way to add durable background jobs to serverless agents.

free-tiers.name: Inngest
free-tiers.description: Durable workflow engine with steps, retries and fan-out — long-running agents that survive restarts.
free-tiers.notes: The most direct fix for 'my agent died halfway through': each step is checkpointed and retried.

free-tiers.name: Trigger.dev
free-tiers.description: Background jobs as code with long-running tasks, realtime progress and observability.

free-tiers.name: Ably
free-tiers.description: Realtime pub/sub and presence for streaming agent output to a browser.

free-tiers.name: Pusher Channels
free-tiers.description: Managed WebSockets with channels, presence and client events.

free-tiers.name: Novu
free-tiers.description: Notification infrastructure that fans out one event to email, in-app, chat and push channels.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30K events/mo on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited

free-tiers.name: CloudAMQP
free-tiers.description: Managed RabbitMQ on a small always-free instance — proper AMQP when QStash is not enough.

free-tiers.name: Langfuse
free-tiers.description: Open-source LLM tracing, prompt management and evaluation — the default for debugging agent runs.
free-tiers.free_limit: 50K observations/mo on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited
free-tiers.notes: Self-hosting on the Oracle always-free ARM VM gives you unlimited tracing for $0.

free-tiers.name: Helicone
free-tiers.description: One-line proxy that logs every LLM request with cost, latency and caching.

free-tiers.name: Sentry
free-tiers.description: Error tracking with stack traces, releases, session replay and an official MCP server.

free-tiers.name: Grafana Cloud
free-tiers.description: Metrics, logs and traces with a permanent free tier plus 14-day retention.

free-tiers.name: Axiom
free-tiers.description: Log analytics built for high-cardinality events, with dashboards and alerts.
free-tiers.notes: 0.5TB/month free is unusually large — useful if you log every agent step and tool call.

free-tiers.name: PostHog
free-tiers.description: Product analytics, session replay, feature flags and experiments in one SDK.

free-tiers.name: Better Stack
free-tiers.description: Uptime monitoring, status pages, on-call alerting and log management.
free-tiers.free_limit: 10 monitors at 3-min checks, 1 status page, 3GB logs

free-tiers.name: UptimeRobot
free-tiers.description: Simple external uptime checks with Slack and email alerts — the guardrail for 'is my agent alive'.

free-tiers.name: Plausible Analytics
free-tiers.description: Privacy-first, cookie-free web analytics — no consent banner needed, GDPR-compliant by design.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30-day trial on cloud; self-hosted Community Edition is free forever
free-tiers.notes: This project's own site should self-host Plausible or Umami — a cookie banner would violate the 'no dark patterns' principle.

free-tiers.name: Umami
free-tiers.description: Lightweight, open-source, cookie-free analytics with a simple dashboard.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (MIT, self-hosted); managed cloud has a small free allowance

free-tiers.name: Resend
free-tiers.description: Transactional email API with React Email templates and good deliverability.

free-tiers.name: Brevo
free-tiers.description: Transactional email plus marketing campaigns and SMS on one generous free plan.

free-tiers.name: Mailtrap
free-tiers.description: Email sandbox for testing plus a small sending allowance — stops agents spamming real inboxes in dev.
free-tiers.free_limit: 1,000 emails/mo sending; free sandbox for testing

free-tiers.name: Algolia
free-tiers.description: Hosted search with typo tolerance, synonyms and instant-search UI libraries.

free-tiers.name: DocSearch
free-tiers.description: Free Algolia-powered documentation search for open-source projects, including crawl and the search UI.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free for open-source and developer documentation
free-tiers.notes: Requires your docs to be public and crawlable — this project's site qualifies.

free-tiers.name: Typesense Cloud
free-tiers.description: Open-source (GPL) search engine with typo tolerance and vector search, self-hostable or managed.
free-tiers.free_limit: Self-hosted is free; cloud offers trial clusters
free-tiers.notes: The managed cloud often lacks a permanent free cluster now — budget to self-host on the free Oracle VM.

free-tiers.name: Actian VectorAI DB (Community Edition)
free-tiers.description: Embedded vector database from Actian that runs on a laptop with no service to deploy, built for agent memory and local RAG prototypes.
free-tiers.notes: Community Edition needs no billing setup and no account. It is an embedded engine, not a hosted service, so there is no cold start or idle shutdown to worry about. Past 5,000 vectors the licence blocks writes but never blocks deletes, so you can always bring a database back into compliance. LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations are published.

free-tiers.name: Wikidata Vector Database
free-tiers.description: Wikimedia Deutschland's public vector database over Wikidata — roughly 30 million knowledge-graph entities exposed as embeddings for RAG grounding in verifiable, open data.
free-tiers.notes: Covers the ~30M Wikidata items that have at least one Wikipedia article, and the current embeddings are built from the September 2024 dump, so treat it as stable-but-not-live data. An API key is still required today; Wikimedia has said future versions will drop that requirement. Pairs with the community Wikidata MCP server at wd-mcp.wmcloud.org.

free-tiers.name: Opik
free-tiers.description: Comet's open-source LLM observability stack — tracing, evaluation, prompt management and production monitoring for agents and RAG pipelines.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, self-host the full platform
free-tiers.notes: The whole platform is Apache-2.0 and self-hostable, so the free tier is not a trimmed demo. Comet also sells a hosted version with a usage allowance if you would rather not run the stack yourself.

free-tiers.name: free-llm-gateway
free-tiers.description: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway that fronts more than a dozen free LLM providers behind one endpoint and falls through to the next provider on failure.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free — self-hosted, bring your own free provider keys
free-tiers.notes: The repository documents 14+ free providers rather than the 24+ that circulates in listicles. It is a small community project (low hundreds of stars) — read the code before putting it in front of real traffic. Pair it with the free tiers already catalogued here (Groq, Gemini, Cerebras, Cloudflare) and the fallback chain rarely runs dry.

free-tiers.name: ClawMetry
free-tiers.description: Real-time observability for a long list of agent runtimes — OpenClaw, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Goose, opencode, Qwen Code, Aider and more — from one dashboard.
free-tiers.notes: Submitted as "12 agent runtimes" and, in an earlier batch, "14". The package itself currently advertises 32, which is typical for this category: the runtime count is a marketing surface, not a spec. Verify your runtime is covered before adopting.

free-tiers.name: agent-observability
free-tiers.description: Local-first tracing for agents that records every tool call, error and dollar spent, and works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP-compatible agent.
free-tiers.notes: Cost tracking per tool call is the feature most local agents still lack. Small community project — read it before wiring it into anything that touches credentials.

free-tiers.name: claw-insights
free-tiers.description: Read-only observability sidecar that tails log files and CLI output, so you get agent tracing with no SDK, no code changes and no network calls.
free-tiers.notes: The zero-instrumentation approach is the whole point: for agents you did not write, or cannot modify, log tailing is the only observation point available.

free-tiers.name: OmniRoute
free-tiers.description: Self-hosted AI router that fans one endpoint out across hundreds of providers, with multiple routing strategies, compression and MCP/A2A support.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted; route to providers' free tiers
free-tiers.notes: Listed in the submission as "160+ providers" and "~1.51B free tokens/month"; the package itself currently advertises 352 providers. Both figures are the vendor's own marketing and the second is not something a gateway can guarantee — it depends entirely on the upstream free tiers, which change without notice.

free-tiers.name: agentgateway
free-tiers.description: Agentic proxy built on the MCP and A2A protocols, adding authentication, observability and governance in front of agents and MCP servers.
free-tiers.notes: A Linux Foundation project with real adoption around MCP, which makes it the most durable entry in this batch. Useful specifically when you need one place to enforce auth and policy across many MCP servers.

free-tiers.name: summoned-gateway
free-tiers.description: OpenAI-compatible gateway with routing, fallback, caching, guardrails and budget limits, with first-class support for Indian providers and INR cost tracking.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free — self-hosted console, bring your own keys
free-tiers.notes: Built-in budget enforcement is the differentiator — a gateway that cannot stop a runaway agent is only half a gateway. Very early project (0.1.x), so expect rough edges.

free-tiers.name: fsrouter
free-tiers.description: Self-hosted gateway that puts one OpenAI-compatible endpoint in front of many providers, with automatic fallback, load balancing and key rotation.
free-tiers.notes: Submitted as "FSRouter"; the package resolves to @fudrouter/fsrouter, whose own description reads "9Router v2 — Monorepo". The naming does not line up cleanly, so verify the package is what you expect before trusting it with provider keys — a gateway holds all of them at once.

free-tiers.name: n9router
free-tiers.description: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible routing gateway for dozens of providers, shipped as a Docker image and usable as a drop-in base URL for the major coding agents.
free-tiers.notes: The submission's repository path (nightwalker8x/n9router) does not exist on GitHub, but the Docker Hub image and npm package both resolve. Prefer the npm release over pulling an unversioned image.

free-tiers.name: Google AI Studio Starter Tier
free-tiers.description: No-card deployment path from AI Studio: prompt an app, click Publish, and get a live Cloud Run URL backed by Firestore or Cloud SQL plus Firebase Auth.
free-tiers.free_limit: Two full-stack apps, no time limit, no billing account
notes: The single best no-card full-stack path in this catalogue — a Google Account is genuinely enough, with no billing account created.
Hard limits: two active apps, 1GiB stored data, 10GiB egress/month, 40K writes and 50K reads a day, one locked-in region, and no BigQuery or Pub/Sub.
You are ineligible if you have ever held a Google Cloud billing account.
Cloud Run scales to zero, so expect a cold start on the first request.

notes: The quota is measured in minutes of GPU time per day and is small (sources report roughly 3.5 minutes authenticated against 2 unauthenticated), so this is for demos and short inference, not training or long-running agents.
Submission claimed the hardware is an RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell; other sources report H200.
Treat the exact GPU as variable — Hugging Face rotates the pool, and the quota is the part that actually constrains you.

free-tiers.name: Databricks Free Edition

free-tiers.free_limit: Forever free, one serverless workspace with daily usage limits
free-tiers.notes: Replaced the retired Community Edition in January 2026 and has no expiry. Non-commercial use only, with a personal email rather than a work one, and Databricks explicitly reserves the right to train on your data — do not put anything proprietary here. No GPUs and no classic compute; it is one serverless workspace with fair-use limits and locked enterprise features.

free-tiers.name: Toolforge

free-tiers.free_limit: Free web servers and job scheduling for Wikimedia tooling
free-tiers.notes: A genuinely hidden free tier that most lists miss. The scope is the catch: it exists for tools that serve the Wikimedia projects, not as general-purpose hosting, and your tool must comply with Wikimedia's tool policies. For a scheduled bot that reads or maintains wiki data, nothing else here comes close on price.

free-tiers.name: Zeabur

notes: Two claims in the submission were wrong in opposite directions, both worth knowing.
Zeabur's free plan requires NO credit card (the submission said it did), and it DOES auto-sleep after inactivity (the submission said it did not) — the wake-up request pays a cold-start penalty.
There is also no SLA on the free plan and no automated database backup, which matters if you treat it as production.
The $5/mo figure quoted as a free credit is actually the price of the paid Dev plan.

free-tiers.free_limit: $100 in credits for AMD AI Developer Program members
notes: Listed as a `trial`, not a free tier.

The submission described this as simply "free" with no card; in fact a valid credit card is required at account creation, the $100 is a one-off credit rather than a rechargeable tier, and the credit hours expire (AMD's own pages disagree — 30 days on the current page, 10 days in older guidance).
Credits apply only to MI300X instances, and you are billed for powered-off instances until you destroy them.
Qualifies under OQ-3 (>= $100 and >= 30 days) and is excluded from every no-card filter.

free-tiers.notes: Listed as a `trial`. The credit runs against standard pay-as-you-go rates for 30 days from activation, so nothing is billed at a fake trial price — what you measure is what production would cost. Hosted entirely in India, which makes it the strongest option here for teams with data-residency requirements. Verify current card requirements at signup: the credit is granted after verification.

A skill URL cannot be checked with a status code: every /skills/<slug> page answers HTTP 200, invented slugs included. Checking one by hand works through the API instead — /api/v1/skills/<slug> returns 404 when a slug does not exist, 409 AMBIGUOUS_SKILL_SLUG when several owners share it, which is why @owner/slug is the only unambiguous reference.

skills.name: Figma Agent Skills
skills.description: Figma's own skill pack for working with design files through its MCP server — implementing designs as code, connecting components with Code Connect, generating design libraries and diagrams, and building Figma slides, FigJam boards, shaders and motion.
notes: 30 skills counted from the repository tree on 2026-09-24: 14 under skills/, the same 14 mirrored under skills-figquery/ for the Figma query variant, and 2 workflow skills. Distribute through Figma's plugins rather than a bare skills/ directory.
Figma marks these a Beta feature, and the pack ships with no repository licence file — check the developer terms before depending on it.
The pack is what the OpenAI curated figma-* skills wrap: same job, published by the vendor whose API it drives.

skills.name: Alireza Rezvani Claude Skills
skills.description: A large community skill library spanning engineering, marketing, product, compliance, finance and C-level advisory work — 388 skills plus custom agents, commands and references, installable across a dozen coding agents.
notes: 388 skills, being the 846 SKILL.md files in the repository tree minus 458 that are mirrors under .gemini/ — 369 skill names appear twice for that reason. The README says '380+' and the skills CLI lists 367, so the true figure sits in that range; 388 is the number the tree supports once mirrors are excluded.
MIT licensed, 26,387 stars, and actively maintained — the largest community pack here after obra/superpowers.

Breadth is the point and also the risk: 388 skills in one repository means most of them are not for you, and a pack this size is a lot of third-party instruction to hand an agent. Install individual skills (--skill <name>) rather than the whole library.

skills.name: A11y Audit
skills.description: An accessibility audit pipeline over WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA: scan, fix and verify, with per-framework fix code and a compliance report. Covers React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, Svelte and plain HTML, and can run the checks in CI.
notes: 934 installs in the skills.sh registry, where it is the second-most-installed result for its name.

Listed on ClawHub in the source dossier but absent there under that slug. This is the real one — verified in the skills.sh registry and in the repository tree, where the skill lives at engineering-team/a11y-audit/skills/a11y-audit alongside a mirrored copy.

skills.name: Notion API
skills.description: Drives a Notion workspace through the REST API with curl and jq rather than a vendor SDK or connector: query a database, create and update pages, and walk blocks, from any agent that can run shell commands.
notes: 78,501 installs in the skills.sh registry — the second-highest of any skill measured for this catalogue, behind only Vercel's find-skills at 3,539,754.
The pack publishes this skill twice, at skills/notion-api/ and plugins/notion-api/skills/, so the CLI's copy and the tree's copy are not the same path.
